$comment: Pins for the real-world WIT the parser is checked against. Read by BOTH
flake.nix (fetchzip, for Nix checkouts) and dev/fetch-wit-corpus.js (for
checkouts without Nix), so the URLs never drift between the two.
Each source is pinned to a commit, not a tag or branch: both can move.
`ref` records what that commit was, for humans.
Two hashes per source, because the two fetchers verify different things:
nixHash        - hash of the UNPACKED tree, what fetchzip wants.
then: nix hash convert --hash-algo sha256 --to sri <hash>
contentDigest  - sha256 over the extracted .wit files (sorted
'relpath sha256(bytes)' lines). Deliberately NOT a hash
of the tarball bytes: GitHub regenerates archives and
the gzip framing changes even when the content does not.
Both fetchers lay the sources out as <root>/<source-name>/…, so the checks
in dev/parse-real-wit.js address them the same way either way.

$why: WASI 0.2 (`wasi:http@0.2.8` and its six vendored deps), plus the
0.3.0-rc-2025-09-16 draft. Vendors its deps under wit/deps/, with the
package header in only one file per package — the layout that exposed
the ordering bugs the synthetic corpus never did. The repo is archived
(merged into WebAssembly/WASI), so this pin will not move again.
Released WASI 0.3.0 — where 0.3 actually lives now. Structurally
different from wasi-http: one wit/ per proposal under proposals/, no
vendored deps at all, so resolving it depends on the topological
package ordering rather than on a deps/ directory.
